topic: Peptides your body makes: carnosine, the muscle's own acid buffer. Carnosine (beta-alanyl-L-histidine) is a dipeptide made in skeletal muscle from beta-alanine and histidine by carnosine synthase, limited by beta-alanine availability; first isolated by Gulewitsch & Amiradzhibi in 1900; the imidazole ring of histidine buffers H+ over the exercise intracellular pH range, from about pH 7.1 at rest to about pH 6 after intense exercise; equine gluteus medius has 6-10 times the carnosine of human muscle (Harris et al., Amino Acids 2012); human muscle carnosine 5-10 mM, type II fibres about 30-100% higher than type I (Jukic et al., Antioxidants 2021)
